newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian shares end easier, watching politics.
newsitem.headline: Italian shares end easier, watching politics.

text.p: Italian shares ended easier on Thursday taking a lead from a lower Wall Street as investors now await further political developments after Wednesday's late parliament vote which kept the centre-left government in power.

Italy's government survived a parliament vote late Wednesday over sending a force to Albania and now looks likely to win votes of confidence later this week. However, dealers said the government had clearly been damaged and overseas investors were wary of the Italian market at the moment.
The MIB30 blue chip index ended off 0.58 percent at 17,776 with the all-share Mibtel down 0.63 percent at 12,002.
Dealers said that with immediate political problems easing, the market was taking its lead from other stock markets, while domestic bonds and the lira moved weaker.

Among main blue chips stocks, Fiat dipped 0.56 percent to 5,460 lire after its new car registrations in March rose, but not as strongly as the whole Italian new car market. While overseas investors were wary after a Turin court late Wednesday handed out suspended sentences to Fiat chairman Cesare Romiti and also its ex-finance director for false accounting.
Shares in cable-making group Sirti rose 175 lire to 10,551 lire after a press report in Il Sole 24 Ore that STET's 48.93 percent stake in Sirti is to be put on the market by the summer.

Olivetti slipped lower on press reports of losses of over 50 billion lire in 1996 at its Telemedia fixed-line telecoms company, which controls its Infostrada telecoms unit. The shares closed off 6.62 percent at 565.5 lire.

It was also undermined by reported remarks by GSM mobile phone operator Omnitel managing director Silvio Scaglia on possible difficulties in reaching its planned break-even in 1998. Olivetti has a 35.5 percent stake in Omnitel.
